signals.title: USD/CHF — G10 Bilateral Theme + Macro
signals.text: USD/CHF trades at 0.7993, falling through its SMA20/50 cluster at 0.8112/0.8081 as the USD remains the broad G10 laggard. The G10 scorecard shows a 2.015% spread between CHF outperformance (+0.862%) and USD weakness (-1.153%), driven by a strong negative U.S. Economic Surprise Index (ESI) of -15.5. While the 375bp Fed-SNB nominal carry advantage structurally favors the USD, current macro momentum is dominated by fading Fed hike bets and increased U.S. Treasury buyback liquidity. Price remains supported above the SMA200 at 0.7930, but the bilateral theme reflects a clear shift in institutional preference away from the greenback. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CHF; broad USD weakness outweighs the nominal carry advantage. Catalyst: SEK interest rate decision 25 Aug. Risk: U.S. data improves, reversing the negative ESI trend and stabilizing the USD.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY at 158.40 is holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (159.91/161.03/158.28), indicating a loss of technical momentum. A 275bp Fed-BoJ nominal carry advantage remains a primary support pillar, yet the options market signals caution with a strong 25d Risk Reversal (RR) of -1.93. This heavy put skew reflects elevated demand for JPY protection despite the carry-supportive spread. While JPY positioning (pctl 73) is not yet extreme, the divergence between the high carry and the aggressive downside hedging in options suggests a fragile bull regime. Trade bias: Neutral USD/JPY; strong downside options hedging counters the carry advantage. Catalyst: next BoJ meeting (mkt: 61% hike priced) 18 Sep — hike bias persistent. Risk: A sustained break back above the SMA50 at 161.03 invalidates the cautious options signal.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7124, maintaining its position above the SMA20/50/200 cluster centered near 0.70. Speculative positioning via COT shows Leveraged Funds net long +45,727 with a WoW add of +7,737, indicating institutional appetite remains firm. This contrasts sharply with retail sentiment, which is currently at an 86% short extreme. This institutional vs. retail divergence typically favors trend continuation as retail traders are forced to cover shorts into price strength. A 60bp AUD carry premium vs the USD further supports the pair amid broad USD weakness. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD; institutional long building against an extreme retail short. Catalyst: next RBA meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) 29 Sep. Risk: A drop below the SMA20 at 0.7041 triggers a broader spec long unwind.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Volatility Premium + Technicals
signals.text: GBP/USD at 1.3611 continues to trade above its SMA20/50/200 cluster (1.3453/1.3386/1.3422), supported by upbeat U.K. CPI data relative to misses in other jurisdictions. The options market displays a significant 5.0% Volatility Risk Premium (VRP), with IV at 11.0% against a realized HV30 of 6.0%. This elevated premium indicates the market is paying a high cost for protection relative to recent price action, reflecting hedging demand around the 1.36 handle. COT positioning is moderately crowded (pctl 90, z +1.23), suggesting the move is well-owned but not yet at an exhaustion extreme. Trade bias: Bullish GBP/USD; supported by technical cluster and high realized-vs-implied volatility spread. Catalyst: next BoE meeting (mkt: 100% hold priced) 17 Sep. Risk: A close below the SMA200 at 1.3422 shifts the technical bias to neutral.
